name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen83
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 3, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: CRYPTO 1-MINUTE MOVES ARE FAR LARGER THAN MODELS EXPECT

The evidence is overwhelming: spreads consistently set 5-15 bps too narrow miss the realized move. Even "quiet" markets move 5-10 bps without warning. The market severely punishes misses and rewards capturing moves.

Failed examples reveal the systematic error:
- Example 1: change_1m -8.2, change_5m -18.6, extreme selling (taker 0.162) → predicted -1.0 ±7.0 bps, actual -4.7 bps → BARELY inside spread
- Example 2: change_1m -3.5, change_5m -17.2, extreme selling (taker 0.16), 60 min to funding, US afternoon → predicted -2.1 ±8.1 bps, actual +3.9 bps → INSIDE but wrong direction after strong reversion
- Example 5: change_1m +1.7, change_5m +2.8, balanced tape, 60 min to funding, US afternoon → predicted -1.2 ±3.2 bps, actual +16.7 bps → CATASTROPHIC MISS (spread 5x too narrow)
- Example 6: change_1m -4.8, change_5m -9.7, selling (taker 0.222), 3am UTC → predicted -0.6 ±5.4 bps, actual +7.3 bps → MISSED by 7.8 bps (strong snapback)
- Example 8: change_1m +0.5, change_5m +3.1, balanced tape, 60 min to funding, Sunday 15 UTC → predicted -1.4 ±1.4 bps, actual -3.3 bps → MISSED (spread 2.3x too narrow)

Pattern: Spreads under 10 bps miss repeatedly. Even small recent moves (|change_1m| < 5) preceded 5-17 bps actual moves. The scoring system severely punishes misses.

MANDATORY MINIMUM SPREADS (half_width_bps):

The absolute floor is 10.0 bps in the quietest conditions. Use these ranges:

BASELINE (half_width 10.0-13.0 bps):
Use ONLY when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 4.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.45-0.55 (balanced tape)
- no bars in last 5 moved >4 bps
- more than 240 minutes from funding
- outside 0-2 UTC, 13-16 UTC hours
- Default: 11.5 bps

MODERATE activity (half_width 13.0-17.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 2.0-5.0 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 4.0-9.0 range
- taker_buy_share in 0.35-0.45 or 0.55-0.65
- 180-300 minutes from funding
- any bar in last 5 moved >4 bps
- Default: 15.0 bps

ELEVATED volatility (half_width 17.0-24.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 5.0-10.0 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 9.0-15.0 range
- taker_buy_share >0.70 or <0.30 (strong imbalance)
- 90-180 minutes from funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13-16 UTC hours (add +3 bps for US hours specifically)
- volume spike (>50% above recent average)
- Default: 20.5 bps

HIGH volatility (half_width 24.0-32.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 10.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 15.0
- taker_buy_share >0.80 or <0.20 (extreme tape)
- 30-90 minutes from funding
- during 13:30-14:30 UTC (US open window)
- multiple consecutive bars >6 bps same direction
- Default: 28.0 bps

VERY HIGH volatility (half_width 32.0-45.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 25.0
- within 30 minutes of funding with signs of positioning
- liquidation cascade (extreme selling + OI drop if visible)
- consecutive bars totaling >30 bps
- after a single bar moved >20 bps (exhaustion snapback risk)
- Default: 38.0 bps

Special context adjustments (ADD to base spread):
- 0-2 UTC: +6 bps (thin liquidity, unpredictable)
- 13-16 UTC: +4 bps baseline, +7 bps during 13:30-14:30 (US open volatility)
- 60-120 min to funding: +4 bps
- 30-60 min to funding: +7 bps
- <30 min to funding: +10 bps
- Extreme tape spike in last bar (>0.85 or <0.15): +5 bps (exhaustion violence)
- After strong move with conflicting signals: +6 bps
- Weekend (Sat/Sun): +3 bps (thinner flow, bigger gaps)

Direction selection with mean reversion priority:
- After |change_1m| > 6, strongly expect reversion; size delta conservatively (0.3-0.5 of the move magnitude)
- After |change_5m| > 12, expect reversion even if last bar continued; the 5m context dominates
- After extreme tape (>0.85 or <0.15) in last bar with move >4 bps, expect consolidation or reversal
- When tape and recent move conflict (e.g., taker_buy 0.2 but change_1m +5), the exhaustion typically snaps toward reversion
- After huge spike (|change_1m| > 15), expect 30-50% retracement in next bar regardless of tape
- When uncertain about direction magnitude, keep |delta_bps| small (1-3 bps) and express doubt via WIDE spread
- When genuinely directionless, set delta near zero but spread VERY WIDE (18-25 bps minimum)

Critical insights from failures:

1. Example 5 disaster: change_1m +1.7, change_5m +2.8, 60 min to funding, 15 UTC → actual +16.7 bps. The ±3.2 bps spread was catastrophically narrow. Funding proximity + US hours demands 20+ bps minimum even when recent moves look small.

2. Example 6: change_1m -4.8, change_5m -9.7, tape 0.222 (selling) → actual +7.3 bps. Strong reversion after -9.7 bps in 5 min. The ±5.4 bps spread missed it entirely. After moves >8 bps in 5 min, spread must be 18+ bps.

3. Example 8: change_1m +0.5, change_5m +3.1, balanced tape, 60 min to funding → actual -3.3 bps. The ±1.4 bps spread was insanely tight. Funding proximity alone demands 15+ bps minimum. Never go below 10 bps.

4. Even after correctly calling direction (Examples 1, 3, 8), spreads 5-7 bps captured barely 50% skill. Spreads must be 2-3x wider than intuition suggests.

Default decision tree:
1. Identify volatility regime from |change_1m|, |change_5m|, tape extremity → set BASE spread
2. Check context: funding proximity, UTC hour, weekend → ADD adjustments
3. Apply minimums: never below 10 bps; funding <120 min never below 15 bps; US hours never below 14 bps
4. Assess direction: default to mean reversion after |change_5m| > 8; mute delta magnitude if conflicting signals
5. Special rules: extreme tape exhaustion, post-spike snapback, funding window positioning
6. Final check: Is my spread wide enough to survive a 2x surprise move? If not, add 5-10 bps
7. Reality check: Compare to recent |change_1m| values in the bars. If your spread is narrower than the largest recent move, you are too tight.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a very confident forecast justifies acting. When in doubt, widen the spread rather than pretend certainty. A wide quote that captures the move scores positive skill; a tight quote that misses scores deeply negative. The market rewards humility and punishes overconfidence ruthlessly.

The systematic error in all failures: underestimating crypto's 1-minute volatility by 2-5x. Correct this and skill improves immediately.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
